![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/94a5da0925a82b91d345fa7811e41c219c19ca48d76b30927e920efed3b2edb3.png)

Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta ),$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $6\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
6\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{12},\frac{\pi }{12}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{12}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{12}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/7f1a9ba1b4d9a86e23b8634dedaf6d4e1a651efbe4fc7aa27ac4dbb5d443018f.png)

Since there are $12$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =12\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =12\cdot 8{\int }_{-\pi /12}^{\pi /12}{cos}^{2}⁡(6\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =96\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /12}^{\pi /12}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(12\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =48{(\theta +\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\theta ))|}_{-\pi /12}^{\pi /12} \\  & =48[(\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))] \\  & =48(\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$
